newsitem.title: CHINA: China's A and B share indices rise on rebound.
newsitem.headline: China's A and B share indices rise on rebound.

text.p: China's A and B share indices rebounded on Friday following losses the previous day, helped by selective buying, brokers said.
The Shanghai B share index rose 0.947 points, or 1.53 percent, to 62.837 points and the Shenzhen B share index gained 1.51 points, or 1.06 percent, to close at 143.16.

In Shanghai, institutional support for shares with a heavy index weighting attracted some follow-up buying, which prevented the index from falling further after losses for three consecutive days, brokers said.
"Today's rebound has improved the technical charts, which will help the market to move steadily around current levels in the short term," a Shanghai broker said.
Market giant Shanghai Diesel Engine rose $0.018, or 3.73 percent, to $0.500 on volume of 973,620 shares.
Market barometer Lujiazui gained $0.030, or 3.70 percent, to $0.840 on volume of 2.1 million shares.
Hua Xin Cement became the star on institutional buying, jumping $0.022, or 9.56 percent, to $0.252 on the day's heaviest volume of 3.8 million shares.

Meanwhile, Shenzhen's B share index closed up due in part to demand for counters promising solid 1996 earnings, with investors shrugging off concerns about Beijing's plan to curb the flow of bank funds into the equity market, brokers said.
"Investors were seen carefully building positions in firms likely to post healthy results for 1996, brokers said.
China Marine Container, Shenzhen's biggest gainer, rose HK$0.28, or 3.22 percent, to HK$8.98 on volume of 335,241 shares due to investor confidence in the company's 1996 profits, brokers said.
Guangdong Power put in the weakest performance and declined HK$0.06 to HK$6.89 on the session's heaviest trade of 1.51 million shares due to institutional selling, brokers said.

The A share indices in both Shanghai and Shenzhen rose on buying in selective shares, with Shanghai's index up 4.771 points, or 0.50 percent, to 959.946 points while Shenzhen's A index advancing 3.76 points, or 1.10 percent, to end at 346.62.
On Shanghai's A share market, Shanghai Steel Tube was the star, jumping 0.56 yuan, or 8.06 percent, to 7.50 yuan on volume of 1.8 million shares.
In Shenzhen, Hubei-based welding materials producer Monkey King was the strongest A share performer, jumping 0.84 yuan, or 9.76 percent, to 9.45 yuan on heavy volume of 14.31 million shares.
